manifest.name: 3D Printers
manifest.description: A 3D Printers tracker: your printers with hotend, extruder, board, firmware, bed size, and local IP. It's a named view of your machines, so each printer still drives prints, fleet status, and maintenance.
manifest.author: Cobblr community
manifest.changelog: A printer's bed size is a fact about its model: once one printer of a model has it, every printer of that model waiting in your inbox gets it too. What was fitted to one printer (its hotend, extruder, mainboard, firmware) stays with that printer.

releases.notes: A printer's bed size is a fact about its model: once one printer of a model has it, every printer of that model waiting in your inbox gets it too. What was fitted to one printer (its hotend, extruder, mainboard, firmware) stays with that printer.
A printer added by name alone (a Bambu Lab P1P, a Prusa MK4) is recognised as a 3D printer and lands in 3D Printers, from its maker and model.

A dropdown says whether a value you type is remembered as a choice for next time; the open ones (a board, a firmware, a controller) offer what you typed before. Setting a service schedule offers the usual jobs (nozzle swap, bed level, belt tension and more) beside the ones you have logged.
Connecting your 3D printers now names every print manager it can send to: Bambu, FDM Monster, OctoPrint, Klipper, Duet or Prusa.

Your 3D printers open the full machine page: set every field (hotend, extruder, mainboard, firmware, bed size, local IP), edit in place, attach files, and link the machine straight to its print manager right from its own page. Installing offers a checked-by-default “Connect to your 3D printers” option that brings the Print Manager along (send a file to be made and track the job), which you can uncheck for catalog-only use. Existing installs auto-upgrade: your 3D printers move into the 3D Printers tab automatically, no reinstall.

features.name: Connect to your 3D printers
features.question: Want to send files to your 3D printers and track the job?
features.description: Adds the Print Manager: map each machine to the software that runs it (Bambu, FDM Monster, OctoPrint, Klipper, Duet or Prusa), send a file to be made, and track the job to completion. Talks to the manager's API; it never drives the hardware. You can link a machine to its manager right from the machine's page.
